note: Phase 2 claims including justice, democracy, public-service, assistance, Popular Sovereignty, and Energy Sovereignty EIA/DOE baselines. Normative claims labeled. No fabricated support.

claims.claim_text: Capitalism has produced broad prosperity across historical contexts.
opposing_evidence: Cross-country and within-country experiences vary widely; distributional outcomes differ.
claims.uncertainty: Too broad for a single Phase 2 quantitative claim; needs scoped historical modules.
claims.public_wording: Market systems have been associated with large gains in material living standards in many contexts, with important exceptions and distributional conflicts.

claims.claim_text: Wage growth and productivity growth have diverged over long periods for typical U.S. workers.
opposing_evidence: Gap size depends on whether average compensation, median wages, or production/nonsupervisory pay is used, and on price deflators.
Some analyses emphasize benefits growth and composition effects.
claims.uncertainty: Causal attribution (market power, technology, globalization, institutions) remains debated.
claims.public_wording: Federal and secondary analyses document a productivity–compensation gap since the 1970s; exact magnitudes depend on measurement choices.

claims.claim_text: Economic concentration can weaken democratic accountability.
opposing_evidence: Concentration measures do not automatically prove political capture.
Countervailing institutions, media, and electoral competition vary.
claims.uncertainty: Needs campaign-finance, lobbying, and media-concentration modules with careful identification.
claims.public_wording: Market concentration is measurable; links from concentration to democratic accountability require additional sourced political-economy research.

claims.claim_text: Employee ownership can improve firm performance and worker outcomes under some conditions.
opposing_evidence: Average performance association is small; many null results exist.
Selection into ESOPs and complementary HR practices confound causal claims.
Employee stock can concentrate retirement risk in one employer.
claims.uncertainty: Design quality (participation, information, diversification) likely mediates outcomes.
claims.public_wording: Research syntheses find employee ownership is often associated with modestly better average performance and stability, not universal improvement.

claims.claim_text: Market concentration can weaken competition in U.S. industries.
opposing_evidence: Rising concentration can reflect efficiency and scale.
National concentration may overstate local rivalry or understate digital competition.
claims.uncertainty: Effects on prices, wages, and entry are industry-specific.
claims.public_wording: The Economic Census publishes concentration ratios showing large-firm shares in many industries; competitive effects must be assessed case by case.

claims.claim_text: Corporate relocation and rural structural decline can drain community capacity, including local banking and healthcare access.
opposing_evidence: Some nonmetro areas have gained population via migration since 2020.
Not all rural counties follow the same path; recreation-adjacent counties differ.
claims.uncertainty: Plant-level relocation causal estimates need separate case/econometric modules.
claims.public_wording: Federal sources document widespread rural county population loss historically, rural hospital closures/conversions, and community-bank charter decline in depopulating areas—alongside recent uneven nonmetro migration gains.

claims.claim_text: AI and automation may increase returns to capital relative to labor and create concentrated adjustment costs.
opposing_evidence: Technology can complement labor and create new tasks; historical automation episodes vary.
claims.uncertainty: Phase 2.1 technology domain; avoid overclaiming.
claims.public_wording: AI’s distributional effects are an open research frontier.

claims.claim_text: Destination-based taxation can better align tax obligations with market access.
opposing_evidence: Administrative complexity; trade and WTO considerations; incidence uncertain.
claims.uncertainty: Normative/policy claim — must not be presented as established fact.
claims.public_wording: A proposed tax-design approach requiring legal and incidence analysis — not an empirical finding.

claims.claim_text: System-level Constitutional Capitalism over 10–20 years would produce larger distributional effects than isolated corporate tax increases.
opposing_evidence: No model results yet; behavioral responses unknown.
claims.uncertainty: Requires modeling; labeled prediction not evidence.
claims.public_wording: A hypothesis for future modeling — not established.

claims.claim_text: Broader ownership participation would shift many households from wage-only dependence toward multi-source capital ownership.
opposing_evidence: Current SCF/DFA show limited bottom-half wealth shares; transition paths unproven.
claims.uncertainty: Depends on adoption, returns, and design.
claims.public_wording: A transition hypothesis; current data show limited bottom-half wealth shares.

claims.claim_text: U.S. household wealth is highly concentrated at the top of the distribution.
opposing_evidence: 2019–2022 SCF showed some narrowing as median rose faster than mean.
DFA top-1% share can move quarter to quarter.
claims.uncertainty: Levels (SCF) and quarterly shares (DFA) are complementary, not identical.
claims.public_wording: Federal data show wealth remains highly concentrated: e.g., DFA Q1 2026 top 1% ≈28.8% and bottom 50% ≈5.3% of wealth; SCF 2022 median net worth $192,900 vs mean $1,063,700.

claims.claim_text: Ordinary households hold a limited share of total household wealth relative to the top decile.
opposing_evidence: Middle 40% (50–90th) still holds a substantial minority share (~31% in Q1 2026 DFA).
claims.uncertainty: Asset composition differs by percentile.
claims.public_wording: In DFA Q1 2026 shares, the top decile holds roughly three-fifths of household wealth while the bottom half holds about one-twentieth.

claims.claim_text: Payroll and individual income taxes are major components of the tax burden on labor income.
opposing_evidence: Economic incidence of payroll taxes may be shared with employers; consumption taxes also burden workers.
Average tax rates and shares depend on CBO’s income definition and how refundable credits are classified.
claims.uncertainty: Needs CBO/Treasury/IRS SOI incidence modules in Phase 2.1.
claims.public_wording: CBO’s 2021 household income/tax distribution shows federal taxes and transfers are major redistributive instruments; labor and capital income composition differs sharply by quintile. Exact payroll vs income-tax incidence modules remain Phase 2.1 work.

claims.claim_text: Statutory corporate taxes may be borne partly by workers and consumers.
opposing_evidence: Incidence estimates vary widely across open-economy models and studies.
claims.uncertainty: Phase 2.1 taxation domain.
claims.public_wording: An open public-finance question — not asserted as settled here.

claims.claim_text: Employer concentration can suppress wages in some labor markets.
opposing_evidence: Effects heterogeneous; measurement of labor-market boundaries contested.
claims.uncertainty: Needs DOJ/FTC/academic monopsony module.
claims.public_wording: Plausible in some markets; not yet sourced as a Phase 2 settled claim.

claims.claim_text: Online commerce can extract spending from local economies via platform concentration and wealth leakage.
opposing_evidence: E-commerce expands consumer choice and can support some local sellers; tax collection rules have changed.
claims.uncertainty: Needs Census e-commerce, platform market-share, and local leakage studies.
claims.public_wording: A priority research question — architecture ready, quantification pending.

claims.claim_text: Property taxation can threaten ownership security for some households.
opposing_evidence: Property tax funds local schools/services; alternatives have their own incidence.
claims.uncertainty: Developing doctrine CC-DEV-003; needs state/local finance evidence.
claims.public_wording: A design concern under research — not a completed empirical proof.

claims.claim_text: Education costs are frequently borne by workers while employers benefit from acquired skills.
opposing_evidence: Workers also capture private returns to education; subsidies already share some costs.
claims.uncertainty: Phase 2.1 education domain.
claims.public_wording: Open research question tied to developing doctrine on human capital.

claims.claim_text: Rural communities face structural barriers to retaining talent, capital, and essential services.
opposing_evidence: Post-2020 migration boosted some nonmetro counties; outcomes diverge sharply by county type.
claims.uncertainty: Aggregate nonmetro gains coexist with majority-county declines.
claims.public_wording: Federal rural data show persistent structural stress (county population loss in many places, hospital closures, community-bank pressures) alongside uneven recent migration gains.

claims.claim_text: Public research contributes to private innovation.
opposing_evidence: Private R&D is also central; attribution of specific products is contested.
claims.uncertainty: Needs NSF/NIH/DOE innovation-linkage module.
claims.public_wording: Queued for sourced innovation research.

claims.claim_text: Equal justice under Constitutional Capitalism cannot depend primarily on wealth.
opposing_evidence: Some argue market-paid counsel is a liberty interest; reform designs vary and public-safety tradeoffs exist in bail systems.
claims.uncertainty: Normative principle recorded as CC-DEV-012; empirical modules on bail, defense, and fees required before policy drafting.
claims.public_wording: Developing doctrine: fundamental justice quality should not turn primarily on ability to pay — evidence modules pending.

claims.claim_text: Justice institutions should not have financial incentives to arrest, charge, detain, supervise, fine, or incarcerate more people.
opposing_evidence: User fees can be framed as cost recovery; empirical magnitude of incentive distortion varies by jurisdiction.
Federal private-prison memos address BOP contracting posture, not a complete empirical map of all fee/forfeiture incentives.
claims.uncertainty: CC-DEV-013/048; CC-SRC-018/019 document federal private-prison policy instability, not national fee/forfeiture magnitudes. Broader sourcing still required before quantitative claims.
claims.public_wording: Developing doctrine: justice should be publicly funded, not financed through the vulnerability of people inside the system — federal private-prison policy history registered; broader sourced examination pending.

claims.claim_text: Economic justice and criminal justice are inseparable because fees, fines, forfeiture, incarceration costs, and collateral consequences transfer power away from individuals and families.
opposing_evidence: Some costs are restitution to victims or legitimate court administration; not all financial consequences are predatory.
claims.uncertainty: Needs linked wealth/ownership and justice baseline modules.
claims.public_wording: Architecture claim: criminal-justice money extraction and exclusion belong inside the national diagnosis — quantification pending.

claims.claim_text: No branch, party, officeholder, donor class, or temporary majority should convert electoral victory into permanent control of the republic.
opposing_evidence: Stable majorities can claim electoral mandates; anti-entrenchment rules can be abused to block legitimate reform.
Strong parties can also organize accountability and opposition.
claims.uncertainty: Normative spine CC-DEV-015/016; empirical modules on entrenchment practices pending.
claims.public_wording: Developing doctrine: political authority is held in trust and must remain returnable — detailed entrenchment evidence modules pending.

claims.claim_text: After Rucho v. Common Cause (2019), partisan-gerrymandering claims are generally nonjusticiable in federal courts as political questions, leaving most partisan-map remedies to Congress, states, commissions, and voters.
opposing_evidence: Dissenting opinions argued federal courts should police extreme partisan gerrymanders.
Racial vote-dilution and one-person-one-vote doctrines remain justiciable and distinct.
claims.uncertainty: State constitutional claims and future congressional action can change the practical landscape without overturning the federal holding.
claims.public_wording: The Supreme Court in Rucho held partisan-gerrymandering claims present political questions beyond federal judicial resolution; reform pathways remain largely political and state-constitutional.

claims.claim_text: Legislative term limits alone are insufficient to prevent political capture and can shift influence toward lobbyists, staff, agencies, and party organizations.
opposing_evidence: Term limits can increase rotation and reduce career entrenchment in some legislatures.
Effects depend on design (consecutive vs lifetime) and complementary transparency rules.
claims.uncertainty: Exact state counts and effect sizes require refreshed primary tables and evaluation literature.
claims.public_wording: NCSL and related experience show term limits are used in a minority of states and are not a complete anti-capture design; complementary transparency and staffing rules matter.

claims.claim_text: Government work should be among the highest forms of civic service; technology should automate routine administration so human talent concentrates in judgment, service, oversight, and engagement.
opposing_evidence: Automation can be used primarily for headcount cuts rather than service elevation.
Some routine administrative work still requires human judgment.
claims.uncertainty: CC-DEV-020/021; needs digital-government and administrative-burden sourcing.
claims.public_wording: Developing doctrine: automate the routine, elevate the human — evidence modules pending; digital-only exclusion forbidden.

claims.claim_text: Every public board, commission, and similar authority should be publicly visible and periodically reviewable for renewal, reform, consolidation, or ending.
opposing_evidence: Some advisory bodies may be temporary by design; overbroad sunset can destroy useful capacity.
Full visibility requirements have administrative costs.
claims.uncertainty: CC-DEV-023; Arkansas Public Authority Inventory is a design agenda, not a completed count.
claims.public_wording: Developing doctrine: invisible boards enable capture — inventory and sunset/renewal architecture pending sourced execution.

claims.claim_text: Digital government services must retain real human access pathways for citizens who are elderly, disabled, rural, poor, offline, or uncomfortable with digital systems.
opposing_evidence: Maintaining parallel channels has cost; poorly designed human pathways can recreate queues and inequity.
claims.uncertainty: Needs digital-exclusion and omnichannel service evaluations.
claims.public_wording: Developing doctrine: automate routine work without abandoning people who cannot or should not be forced online-only.

claims.claim_text: Government should continuously reduce administrative friction while continuously improving public service — eliminating waste without treating service reduction or headcount cuts as ends in themselves.
opposing_evidence: Some friction is deliberate oversight; aggressive simplification can weaken legitimate safeguards.
Burden-reduction targets can be gamed as paper compliance.
claims.uncertainty: CC-DEV-025; needs administrative-burden and life-event service evaluations. 80/20 routine/judgment split is a heuristic, not a measured universal fact.
claims.public_wording: Developing doctrine: reduce friction, improve service — not more vs less government as the only frame.

claims.claim_text: Government should become invisible in bureaucracy — services work without citizens noticing friction — but never unaccountable: every decision remains explainable, reviewable, measurable, auditable, and constitutionally limited.
opposing_evidence: Opacity is sometimes defended as protecting deliberation or security.
Usability reforms can mask weak accountability if dashboards are PR-only.
claims.uncertainty: CC-DEV-026 iconic phrase; needs citizen-experience and accountability-integrity modules.
claims.public_wording: Iconic developing doctrine: government should become invisible—but never unaccountable.

claims.claim_text: Government should operate as a coordinated platform that collects verified information once and reuses it securely with appropriate legal authorization, organized around citizen life events rather than agency silos.
opposing_evidence: Interagency data reuse without strong consent and authorization can violate privacy and due process.
Central portals can become single points of failure or surveillance risk.
claims.uncertainty: CC-DEV-027; needs identity, consent, and interagency legal frameworks.
claims.public_wording: Developing doctrine: collect once, reuse securely with legal authorization; citizen sees one journey.

claims.claim_text: AI may assist government by reducing routine work, but must never become the final decision-maker on matters affecting legal rights or significant benefits; final judgment remains with accountable officials.
opposing_evidence: Some jurisdictions already use high-stakes automated scoring; defining ‘significant benefits’ requires legal precision.
Human-in-the-loop can become rubber-stamping without real review capacity.
claims.uncertainty: CC-DEV-028; needs public-sector AI governance and due-process literature.
claims.public_wording: Developing doctrine: AI assists; accountable humans decide rights and significant benefits.

claims.claim_text: Government information created with public resources should be presumed open unless there is a constitutionally or legally justified reason to protect it; the burden should generally be on the government to explain withholding.
opposing_evidence: Some jurisdictions default to broad exemptions that function as secrecy.
Absolute openness can conflict with privacy, safety, and national security obligations.
claims.uncertainty: CC-DEV-029; needs open-records exception inventories and appeal-practice modules.
claims.public_wording: Developing doctrine: presumed open, justified exceptions, government bears the burden of explanation.

claims.claim_text: Every government action funded or authorized by the public should leave a digital trail through a constitutional accountability ledger — the People's Ledger — linking authority, purpose, cost, contracts, audits, and outcomes.
opposing_evidence: Building unified ledgers has cost and cybersecurity risk.
Fragmented legacy systems make end-to-end trails difficult without phased modernization.
claims.uncertainty: CC-DEV-031; People's Ledger is a design agenda — do not invent portal coverage rates.
claims.public_wording: Developing doctrine: the People's Ledger — every public dollar and major action has a searchable story.

claims.claim_text: Routine public records should be freely accessible without unnecessary identity barriers; sensitive or high-volume access may require authentication or rate limits; actions that change government records must always be authenticated and audited; free public-access terminals should support equal access.
opposing_evidence: Anonymous high-volume scraping can create security and privacy risks.
Terminal programs require funding and maintenance.
claims.uncertainty: CC-DEV-032; needs portal identity-policy and public-terminal evaluations.
claims.public_wording: Developing doctrine: open routine access without chilling ID rules; authenticate changes; equal offline access.

claims.claim_text: AI should help citizens understand public records as an interpreter, while the underlying records remain the official source of truth.
opposing_evidence: AI summaries can hallucinate or omit context if not citation-bound.
Over-reliance on AI can reduce direct engagement with primary records.
claims.uncertainty: Needs civic AI evaluation with mandatory citation to official records.
claims.public_wording: Developing doctrine: AI interprets; official records remain authoritative.

claims.claim_text: Essential systems such as banking, insurance, and healthcare should be evaluated through system design and incentive alignment — rewarding private innovation while protecting the public interest — rather than beginning from conclusions of inherent corruption.
opposing_evidence: Some sectors show repeated misconduct patterns that can justify heightened scrutiny.
System-design framing can understate concentrated political influence if capture is not measured.
claims.uncertainty: CC-DEV-033; sector modules pending Phase 2.1 sourcing.
claims.public_wording: Developing doctrine: design essential systems with shared questions — do not start from inherent-corruption conclusions.

claims.claim_text: The financial system should primarily reward the creation of productive value rather than the extraction of value.
opposing_evidence: Risk allocation, liquidity provision, and hedging can create real economic value even when not tied to a single tangible asset.
Definitions of productive vs extractive finance are contested.
claims.uncertainty: CC-DEV-034; needs lending-composition and community-finance evidence modules.
claims.public_wording: Developing doctrine: finance should primarily reward productive value creation — research before detailed banking law.

claims.claim_text: Healthy citizens are one of society's greatest strengths; a constitutional republic should measure success not only by treating illness, but by helping people remain healthy — including through community health measurement and prevention.
opposing_evidence: Prevention programs vary widely in effectiveness and cost-effectiveness.
Some health outcomes are driven by factors outside community control.
claims.uncertainty: CC-DEV-035; Community Health Index is a design agenda — no invented scores. Do not assert unsupported claims that pharmaceuticals are designed to keep people sick.
claims.public_wording: Developing doctrine: measure health maintenance, not only illness treatment; Community Health Index pending evidence design.

claims.claim_text: A preventive society should gradually shift public investment from paying for avoidable crises toward preventing those crises across healthcare, education, justice, infrastructure, disaster preparedness, environment, and economic development.
opposing_evidence: Prevention benefits can be hard to attribute and politically undervalued.
Not all prevention spending outperforms treatment or response at the margin.
claims.uncertainty: CC-DEV-036; needs cross-domain prevention evaluations.
claims.public_wording: Developing doctrine: invest in preventing avoidable crises — measure averted harms, do not assume automatic savings.

claims.claim_text: Every child should graduate with a meaningful pathway to productive adulthood through multiple respected pathways of equal dignity rather than a single model of success.
opposing_evidence: Labor-market returns differ across pathways and change over time.
Equal dignity does not erase the need for rigorous standards in each pathway.
claims.uncertainty: CC-DEV-038; pathway outcome modules pending.
claims.public_wording: Developing doctrine: multiple respected pathways of equal dignity — not a single success model.

claims.claim_text: A constitutional republic should deliberately build human capital infrastructure — institutions that produce capable, healthy, innovative citizens — with the same seriousness as physical infrastructure.
opposing_evidence: Human-capital investments vary widely in return and can be captured by credentials without skill.
Physical infrastructure remains necessary and competing budget claims are real.
claims.uncertainty: CC-DEV-039; needs regional skill-gap and return-to-skill modules.
claims.public_wording: Developing doctrine: build human infrastructure as deliberately as highways and broadband.

claims.claim_text: Regional civic and innovation academies organized around regional economic strengths are a promising institutional model for making home stronger and should be researched and piloted before any statewide lock-in.
opposing_evidence: Residential academies have cost, access, and selection challenges.
Regional specialization can under-serve students whose interests differ from local industries if mobility across academies is weak.
claims.uncertainty: CC-DEV-040; design agenda — no invented enrollment or retention outcomes. ASMSA is an institutional reference, not a sourced proof in this slice.
claims.public_wording: Developing doctrine: pilot regional academies that make home stronger — research before statewide design lock-in.

claims.claim_text: Human capital pathways should combine paid real-world work, entrepreneurship of equal seriousness to trades, and civic leadership formation, and should be measured by flourishing outcomes beyond graduation rates.
opposing_evidence: Apprenticeship and entrepreneurship programs vary in quality and scale.
Civic curriculum can become performative without practice opportunities.
claims.uncertainty: CC-DEV-041; metric agenda only — no invented earnings or business-start rates.
claims.public_wording: Developing doctrine: real work, entrepreneurship, civic leadership — measure flourishing, not only graduation.

claims.claim_text: The signature of Constitutional Capitalism should be adaptive community playbooks that answer how a real town can strengthen and grow over decades — same principles, different local implementation — rather than stopping at what government should do.
opposing_evidence: Some national rules require uniformity; local playbooks cannot contradict constitutional rights.
Playbook libraries can become bureaucratic if not kept adaptive and evidence-linked.
claims.uncertainty: CC-DEV-042; illustrative growth questions (e.g., 500 to 5,000) are design aspirations, not forecasts.
claims.public_wording: Developing doctrine: playbooks for real communities — same principles, different implementation.

claims.claim_text: Constitutional Capitalism should operate as a layered architecture connecting philosophy, constitution, research, implementation, a Community Operating System, national measurement, and continuous civic improvement.
opposing_evidence: Multi-layer systems can become organizationally heavy if productized too early.
Community OS features require security, privacy, and governance design before launch.
claims.uncertainty: CC-DEV-043; Community OS is a design agenda, not an operating product.
claims.public_wording: Developing doctrine: philosophy through civic improvement as one connected operating architecture.

claims.claim_text: Community implementation should begin with assets and people, then attract talent, keep people, and expand ownership through local prosperity engines and resilient many-owner/employer ecosystems.
opposing_evidence: Some places lack sufficient local assets without outside capital or infrastructure investment.
Small-business ecosystems can still fail without demand, skills, and finance.
claims.uncertainty: CC-DEV-044; illustrative job arithmetic is design discussion only, not a case result.
claims.public_wording: Developing doctrine: assets and people first; attract, keep, and make owners.

claims.claim_text: No proposal within Constitutional Capitalism is complete until it includes an implementation pathway, measurable outcomes, estimated costs, anticipated tradeoffs, and a process for evaluation and revision.
opposing_evidence: Early-stage philosophical concepts may not yet support full cost estimates; the rule should scale with maturity.
Over-rigid completeness gates can block useful exploratory research if misapplied.
claims.uncertainty: CC-DEV-045; apply proportionally — exploratory research may mark missing fields explicitly rather than fake precision.
claims.public_wording: Permanent rule: pathway, outcomes, costs, tradeoffs, evaluation — or the proposal is incomplete.

claims.claim_text: Public safety belongs to the community, and a complete Community Safety and Restoration System should prevent harm, respond quickly, protect victims, treat addiction and mental illness, hold dangerous people securely, restore everyone who can be restored, and return as many people as safely possible to productive citizenship — not merely be softer or tougher on crime.
opposing_evidence: Some argue specialized police agencies alone are sufficient without a broader corps model.
Public-safety and incapacitation literatures warn that restoration framing can underweight violence risk if poorly designed.
claims.uncertainty: CC-DEV-046; system architecture before offense-specific statutes; no invented crime rates.
claims.public_wording: Developing doctrine: community safety is a complete system — prevent, protect, treat, secure, restore, return.

claims.claim_text: Local public safety should be organized as a Community Safety Corps coordinating sworn officers with community officers, behavioral-health responders, restoration officers, and victim-service officers, building on community-policing elements of partnerships, problem-solving, and organizational transformation while separating noncoercive community service from armed enforcement.
opposing_evidence: Civilianization and co-responder models vary widely in effectiveness by design, funding, and crisis type.
Some rural jurisdictions may lack clinician supply for dedicated behavioral-health teams without regionalization.
claims.uncertainty: CC-DEV-047; COPS definition supports three community-policing elements; Corps staffing model remains a design agenda pending local capacity research.
claims.public_wording: Developing doctrine: Community Safety Corps — more presence, right profession for the task; arrest quotas banned.

claims.claim_text: The state may not create a private financial interest in keeping human beings incarcerated; private prisons, jails, or probation firms should not be paid by occupied beds, confinement length, supervision volume, or collected fees, while supporting vendor services may remain private under public custody and release authority.
opposing_evidence: Some argue private operators can expand capacity faster or at lower short-term cost; comparative quality evidence is contested.
Federal memos do not by themselves prove optimal state/local contracting rules.
claims.uncertainty: CC-DEV-048; CC-SRC-018/019 show 2016 Yates phase-down and 2017 Sessions rescission (not a 2023 rescission). Later EO/policy churn may continue; principle should be settled in law. No invented privatization market-share stats.
claims.public_wording: Developing doctrine: no private financial interest in human confinement; settle the principle in law.

claims.claim_text: Justice intake should route people onto proportionate pathways (serious danger; nonviolent accountability; addiction-driven conduct; mental-health crisis; poverty-related technical violations), with prisons as secure restoration campuses, reentry beginning during confinement, and productive citizenship as the destination after sentence completion — evaluated rigorously because reentry-program effects are often modest and mixed.
opposing_evidence: Treatment and mental-health courts are not appropriate for every defendant; net-widening risks exist.
Some evaluations find only modest short-term reentry gains; programs are not magical.
Secure confinement remains necessary for demonstrated substantial threats.
claims.uncertainty: CC-DEV-049; BJA/NIJ sources support model elements and measurement caution, not a single national pathway statute. Distinguish inability from refusal without inventing jail-for-debt prevalence figures.
claims.public_wording: Developing doctrine: right pathway, restoration campuses, reentry from day one, citizenship destination — evaluate honestly.

claims.claim_text: Constitutional Capitalism should never classify people as unworthy of reentry; the correct category for continuing extreme danger is people whose current, demonstrated danger requires continuing secure custody, because no person loses human dignity even when they lose liberty.
opposing_evidence: Some political rhetoric treats permanent moral unworthiness as a deterrent message; that framing conflicts with dignity-centered constitutional design.
claims.uncertainty: CC-DEV-050; philosophical and institutional design claim; legal review needed for operational definition of continuing extreme danger.
claims.public_wording: Developing doctrine: never unworthy of reentry — judge current demonstrated danger and required restriction, not human worth.

claims.claim_text: When continuing extreme danger cannot be safely managed in the community after due process and repeated review, the response should be publicly operated Secure Public Safety Campuses providing humane permanent incapacitation with continuing review, graduated custody, and earned pathways even when release is unlikely — not exile, abandonment, or private imprisonment.
opposing_evidence: Some argue ordinary maximum-security prisons already suffice without a specialized campus model.
Periodic review can be attacked as creating false hope or political pressure for unsafe release.
claims.uncertainty: CC-DEV-051; campuses are a design agenda; Eighth Amendment conditions sourcing needs legal-review completion (Constitution Annotated retrieval blocked at registration).
claims.public_wording: Developing doctrine: Secure Public Safety Campuses — public, humane, productive, reviewable continuing custody.

claims.claim_text: A risk-assessment score alone should never authorize permanent secure custody; validated, bias-reviewed tools may structure decisions only when combined with individualized professional and judicial judgment under narrow eligibility standards.
opposing_evidence: Actuarial tools often outperform unstructured professional judgment on average predictive accuracy, which some use to argue for heavier reliance on scores.
Tool quality and local validation vary widely.
claims.uncertainty: CC-DEV-051; BJA/PSRAC explains probabilistic nature and validity variation — supports score-plus-judgment rule, not abolition of risk tools.
claims.public_wording: Developing doctrine: risk tools may inform; scores alone never decide permanent custody.

claims.claim_text: Expensive secure custody should be concentrated on people who truly require it; permanent confinement must reject exile/banishment and private profit from longer stays, while aging and medical status can justify lower security or medical secure care because federal reviews show high medical costs for aging populations and generally lower misconduct and rearrest among older cohorts — without inventing automatic release.
opposing_evidence: Some older individuals remain highly dangerous; averages do not control individual cases.
Compassionate-release and elderly programs have narrow eligibility and uneven use.
Private operators argue capacity and cost advantages that remain contested.
claims.uncertainty: CC-DEV-052; GAO-17-379 supports aging health-care cost pressure; DOJ OIG 15-05 supports lower average misconduct/rearrest for aging federal inmates; FSA FAQ shows federal mechanisms exist. State systems and individual dangerousness require separate modules.
claims.public_wording: Developing doctrine: concentrate secure custody where required; no exile; no private profit from keeping people longer; age/medical status can change security level.

claims.claim_text: Natural resources belong first to the place that bears the extraction, consumption, congestion, pollution, and long-term risk; private enterprise may profit from using them, but the affected community must receive a direct, permanent, and measurable return, with obligation rising as consumption, scarcity, risk, or damage rises.
opposing_evidence: Some argue national or statewide resource ownership better manages strategic minerals and interstate externalities.
Permit-and-tax systems already exist in many jurisdictions; comparative effectiveness varies.
claims.uncertainty: CC-DEV-053; central doctrine before statutes; no invented rent or royalty statistics.
claims.public_wording: Central doctrine: resources belong first to the place that bears the burden — private profit allowed, community return required.

claims.claim_text: Large resource-consuming projects should negotiate a binding Community Resource Compact with progressive essential-to-transformative pricing and total-footprint disclosure including Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions, and should pass a Community Carrying-Capacity Test before public approval or infrastructure access.
opposing_evidence: Complex compact negotiation can slow beneficial investment if poorly designed.
Scope accounting methods and boundary choices can be gamed without independent audit.
claims.uncertainty: CC-DEV-054; EPA Scope 1/2 guidance supports disclosure distinction; Compact mechanics remain design agenda.
claims.public_wording: Developing doctrine: Community Resource Compact + progressive pricing + full footprint + Carrying-Capacity Test.

claims.claim_text: The majority of geographically concentrated impact revenue must return to the affected place through protected household, infrastructure, restoration, and Future Generations accounts, and exceptionally large projects should also provide continuing community ownership interests rather than only negotiable one-time fees.
opposing_evidence: Statewide pooling can fund broader resilience and equalization.
Community equity can complicate financeability for some projects.
claims.uncertainty: CC-DEV-055; illustrative percentage splits require modeling and are not locked rates.
claims.public_wording: Developing doctrine: majority of impact revenue stays local; Future Generations Fund; community equity for exceptional projects.

claims.claim_text: Data centers, mineral extraction, and large warehouses require sector-specific Compacts; residential customers should never subsidize extraordinary corporate infrastructure or electricity discounts; mining must include bankruptcy-proof cleanup; and a durable Resource and Pollution Ledger should outlast changeable federal GHG reporting rules.
opposing_evidence: Some jurisdictions intentionally discount industrial power to attract investment; net local welfare effects are contested.
Federal CAA data-center resources emphasize permitting clarity and development speed as well as transparency.
claims.uncertainty: CC-DEV-056; GHGRP continuity is politically changeable (including proposed reconsideration noted by EPA); do not invent rate or cleanup-bond figures.
claims.public_wording: Developing doctrine: sector Compacts; no household subsidy of extraordinary corporate loads; bankruptcy-proof cleanup; durable pollution ledger.

claims.claim_text: High-emitting entities should finance locally verified ecological restoration through a Local Carbon Restoration Exchange under an anti-fraud hierarchy that prioritizes avoidance and reduction before offsets, with verified baselines, independent measurement, permanence, and no double counting.
opposing_evidence: Measurement uncertainty and permanence risk can undermine soil-carbon payment schemes.
Voluntary credit markets have documented quality problems when verification is weak.
claims.uncertainty: CC-DEV-057; USDA/NRCS practice recognition and FSA soil-carbon monitoring support measurement emphasis, not a claim that every practice sequesters a known quantity.
claims.public_wording: Developing doctrine: pay regenerative farms for verified local value; offsets never excuse unlimited pollution.

claims.claim_text: Communities should expand community-owned energy — including community solar and other local generation/storage where appropriate — and protect a household essential-electricity floor at the lowest sustainable price, while extraordinary commercial use pays its full marginal and community cost.
opposing_evidence: Local generation does not eliminate the need for regional grid reliability.
Essential-use block rates require careful design to avoid waste or cost-shifting.
claims.uncertainty: CC-DEV-057; DOE community-solar definition supports multi-customer local benefit models; microgrids and other technologies need separate modules.
claims.public_wording: Developing doctrine: community-owned energy + household energy floor; extraordinary commercial use pays full cost.

claims.claim_text: Food is critical infrastructure; every community should have capacity to provide a meaningful share of essential food needs while remaining connected to broader markets for resilience and opportunity, and Constitutional Capitalism rejects an export-only rule for mass-produced staples.
opposing_evidence: Some argue maximum specialization and distant markets alone minimize cost.
Local capacity targets can be hard to define for arid or short-season regions.
claims.uncertainty: CC-DEV-058; ERS defines food security as access; place-based production capacity is an extension requiring local modules. No invented insecurity rates.
claims.public_wording: Developing doctrine: food as infrastructure — local capacity plus open markets; never export-only staples.

claims.claim_text: Regional Food Networks and a State Food Exchange should operate as logistics infrastructure — not government grocery stores — improving small-producer market access, institutional fresh-food purchasing, and local value-added processing under a Local First, Export Second opportunity principle.
opposing_evidence: Food hubs and local markets vary widely in viability and scale.
Institutional procurement rules can block local purchasing even when platforms exist.
claims.uncertainty: CC-DEV-059; USDA LAMP supports local/regional and value-added goals; Exchange remains a design agenda.
claims.public_wording: Developing doctrine: logistics platform and regional networks — not government grocery stores; keep value local.

claims.claim_text: Wasted food should be treated as wasted human effort; surplus should move preferentially to people and emergency reserves, and regions should maintain emergency food capacity without replacing private markets.
opposing_evidence: Donation logistics have liability, quality, and transportation constraints.
Poorly designed reserves can spoil or distort markets if mismanaged.
claims.uncertainty: CC-DEV-060; EPA Wasted Food Scale ranks prevention/donation highly but does not design reserve systems; no invented waste percentages.
claims.public_wording: Developing doctrine: surplus feeds people and reserves first; emergency capacity without replacing markets.

claims.claim_text: Farmers who improve verified soil health, water quality, biodiversity, and carbon storage should be eligible for payments tied to public benefits, connecting Community Food Security to Resource Sovereignty restoration exchanges.
opposing_evidence: Measurement and permanence challenges can undermine payment integrity.
Not all farms can participate equally across soil types and climates.
claims.uncertainty: CC-DEV-060 linked to CC-DEV-057; verification protocols still required.
claims.public_wording: Developing doctrine: pay verified regenerative public value — linked to Resource Sovereignty.

claims.claim_text: Community Food Security requires food education and a public Community Food Dashboard tracking local/regional sourcing, access, affordability, farmer income, waste, reserves, nutrition, and processing capacity without inventing outcomes before sources exist.
opposing_evidence: Local-sourcing percentage metrics are hard to define and compare across places.
Dashboards can create false precision if data quality is weak.
claims.uncertainty: CC-DEV-061; ERS/AMS tools support measurement agendas; indicator slots remain null until sourced.
claims.public_wording: Developing doctrine: teach food systems; measure honestly on a Community Food Dashboard.

claims.claim_text: Every person stands equal before the Constitution; wealth, office, race, religion, political affiliation, social status, birthplace, celebrity, and institutional influence must neither increase nor diminish legal protection or legal accountability.
opposing_evidence: Historical and contemporary systems often exhibit unequal protection or selective accountability in practice.
Role-specific duties and age-based rules show that identical treatment of every situation is not the same as equal standing.
claims.uncertainty: CC-DEV-062 / CC-PRIN-29; complementary to Declaration On equality (rejects outcome equality); empirical enforcement patterns Phase 2.1+.
claims.public_wording: Foundational principle: equal standing before the Constitution — equal protection and equal accountability.

claims.claim_text: Justice should evaluate conduct before identity whenever constitutionally and practically possible (Blind Stage Principle), while acknowledging that identity can be legally relevant for proof of who acted or for laws that depend on age or professional status.
opposing_evidence: Some proceedings necessarily involve identity facts early (identification, jurisdiction, capacity).
Taken literally, 'hear evidence before seeing the person' is not always procedurally possible.
claims.uncertainty: CC-DEV-063; iconic phrase is guiding philosophy, not a literal universal courtroom protocol.
claims.public_wording: Developing doctrine: evaluate conduct before status whenever possible — Blind Stage Principle.

claims.claim_text: Equal constitutional opportunity and equal accountability are paired: no one is above the law, and no one is beneath its protection.
opposing_evidence: Immunities, prosecutorial discretion, and resource gaps can create practical inequality even under formal equality rules.
claims.uncertainty: CC-DEV-064; institutional design and measurement modules required.
claims.public_wording: Developing doctrine: equal opportunity paired with equal accountability.

claims.claim_text: Constitutional Capitalism rejects privilege in every direction — corporate, political, bureaucratic, inherited governmental, wealth-based, and influence-based privilege, including selective enforcement — and also rejects arbitrary discrimination against people because they belong to any particular group.
opposing_evidence: Some legal privileges (e.g., legislative speech protections) exist for institutional reasons and require careful constitutional analysis rather than blanket abolition rhetoric.
claims.uncertainty: CC-DEV-065; distinguish illegitimate status privilege from constitutionally justified role protections.
claims.public_wording: Developing doctrine: reject privilege and arbitrary discrimination; Constitution as common standard.

claims.claim_text: Equal justice requires meaningful access to competent legal representation, understandable laws, public records, government services, appeals, and due process; otherwise equality exists only on paper.
opposing_evidence: Access systems vary widely by jurisdiction; minimum standards are contested.
Resource constraints can make universal competent representation difficult without tradeoffs.
claims.uncertainty: CC-DEV-066; design agenda — do not invent representation rates or delay statistics.
claims.public_wording: Developing doctrine: equal justice requires equal access, not paper rights alone.

claims.claim_text: A healthy constitutional culture treats people as fellow citizens first under a common legal standard: diversity is real; equality under the law is non-negotiable.
opposing_evidence: Identity and group affiliation are politically and culturally salient; civic-identity appeals do not automatically reduce conflict.
claims.uncertainty: CC-DEV-067; cultural claim, not an empirical prediction of harmony.
claims.public_wording: Developing doctrine: fellow citizens first; equality under law non-negotiable.

claims.claim_text: Self-government requires education; a constitutional republic has a duty to prepare every generation to understand rights, responsibilities, institutions, and peaceful civic improvement — treating democracy as a skill learned through experience, not merely a right activated by age.
opposing_evidence: Some traditions emphasize formal legal adulthood thresholds more than continuous civic pedagogy.
Civic-education effects on adult behavior are heterogeneous across programs and contexts.
claims.uncertainty: CC-DEV-068 / CC-PRIN-30; architecture before sourced outcome modules.
claims.public_wording: Core doctrine: self-government requires education; democracy is a skill.

claims.claim_text: Civic education should begin in elementary school through participation (debate, voting practice, budgeting, problem-solving, community projects) along a developmental pathway from community awareness to applied citizenship by graduation.
opposing_evidence: Age-band curricula can become rigid or uneven across districts.
Participatory programs require teacher capacity and community partnerships that are not universal.
claims.uncertainty: CC-DEV-069; pathway is design agenda, not locked national curriculum.
claims.public_wording: Developing doctrine: practice democracy from elementary school along a developmental pathway.

claims.claim_text: Communities should create real Youth Leadership Councils through which students advise local institutions and organize projects while adults remain legally responsible.
opposing_evidence: Youth councils can become symbolic if adults ignore recommendations.
Legal and liability boundaries must remain clear.
claims.uncertainty: CC-DEV-070; design agenda — not operating government authority for minors.
claims.public_wording: Developing doctrine: real Youth Leadership Councils; adults remain legally responsible.

claims.claim_text: Earlier voting eligibility should not be declared as a settled age rule; instead, preparation-conditioned local participation models (for example, certified civic-curriculum completers in school board/municipal/local ballot elections) should be piloted and evaluated before broader adoption, leaving federal and statewide elections unchanged unless future evidence supports reform.
opposing_evidence: Reasonable people disagree on voting age as a matter of principle independent of curriculum.
Certification regimes can become gatekeeping or politicized.
Youth local-voting effects on lifelong turnout and institutional trust are contested/unsettled.
claims.uncertainty: CC-DEV-071; exploratory model only — no invented youth-voting outcome statistics.
claims.public_wording: Developing doctrine: explore preparation-conditioned local participation pilots — do not lock voting at 16.

claims.claim_text: Students should graduate civically as well as academically through a Constitutional Citizenship Portfolio demonstrating service, constitutional knowledge, budgeting, public speaking, teamwork, media literacy, problem solving, a civic project, and leadership experience.
opposing_evidence: Portfolio requirements can become checkbox compliance without authentic learning.
Resource disparities across schools can make portfolio quality uneven.
claims.uncertainty: CC-DEV-072; design agenda with authenticity safeguards required.
claims.public_wording: Developing doctrine: Civic Graduation via Constitutional Citizenship Portfolio.

claims.claim_text: Schools should operate as community civic laboratories, teenagers should complete meaningful civic service as contribution rather than punishment, and experiential civic scorecards should track practice (meetings, presentations, volunteering, organizing, budgeting, Constitution literacy) rather than letter-grade theater.
opposing_evidence: School-as-community-center models require staffing, security, and partnership capacity.
Experience tracking can become surveillance if poorly designed.
claims.uncertainty: CC-DEV-073; design agenda — no invented service-completion rates.
claims.public_wording: Developing doctrine: schools as civic laboratories; service as contribution; experience scorecards.

claims.claim_text: Every student should complete meaningful civic service that strengthens democratic participation while preserving complete freedom to choose causes and viewpoints; public education should remain neutral toward parties, candidates, and viewpoints, and government should encourage participation, not ideology.
opposing_evidence: Some service-learning programs historically blur civic and partisan aims.
Defining and auditing viewpoint neutrality in school credit systems is administratively difficult.
claims.uncertainty: CC-DEV-074 / CC-PRIN-31; architecture before compliance-pattern research.
claims.public_wording: Developing doctrine: civic participation, not partisan conformity; encourage participation, not ideology.

claims.claim_text: Students should earn Civic Service Credits through a multi-pathway Civic Service Portfolio covering government participation, community improvement, and civic engagement, rather than traditional volunteer hours alone.
opposing_evidence: Multi-pathway portfolios can become checkbox compliance without authentic learning.
Access to meetings, internships, and projects varies by community capacity.
claims.uncertainty: CC-DEV-075; design agenda — no invented completion rates.
claims.public_wording: Developing doctrine: Civic Service Portfolio with multiple credit pathways.

claims.claim_text: Optional political or campaign activity may count toward civic credit only under viewpoint-neutral equal standards; schools may not require students to support or oppose any candidate, party, or policy position as a condition of graduation, and students must be able to satisfy the same requirement through nonpartisan alternatives.
opposing_evidence: Some argue any school recognition of campaign work risks entanglement; others argue exclusion of political activity is itself viewpoint-restrictive.
Equal-standards administration can be contested in practice.
claims.uncertainty: CC-DEV-076; legal-review package required before school-policy drafting.
claims.public_wording: Developing doctrine: optional campaign credit only under equal viewpoint-neutral standards; never required.

claims.claim_text: Civic experiences should include reflection focused on democratic practice and evidence rather than predetermined conclusions, and graduates may receive a Civic Achievement Transcript documenting civic merit experiences rather than political conformity.
opposing_evidence: Reflection prompts can be written or graded in ways that favor preferred conclusions.
Transcripts raise privacy and authenticity concerns if poorly designed.
claims.uncertainty: CC-DEV-077; design agenda with neutrality and privacy safeguards.
claims.public_wording: Developing doctrine: reflection for learning; Civic Achievement Transcript for civic merit, not ideology.

claims.claim_text: A nation's greatest long-term asset is the children it raises; children are the shared responsibility of families, communities, and ultimately the republic until prepared to become healthy, capable, independent participants — with inherent dignity independent of economic output.
opposing_evidence: Some policy traditions emphasize state institutions as primary childhood systems.
Measuring 'preparation for independent participation' can be contested.
claims.uncertainty: CC-DEV-078 / CC-PRIN-32; reject productive-as-worth language.
claims.public_wording: Foundational principle: children are the greatest long-term asset — with inherent dignity.

claims.claim_text: Strong families create strong communities and a strong republic; public institutions should strengthen families rather than replace them whenever possible, with support climbing a subsidiarity care ladder.
opposing_evidence: Some children lack safe family environments; nearer supports can fail.
Subsidiarity thresholds are hard to operationalize.
claims.uncertainty: CC-DEV-079 / CC-DEV-080.
claims.public_wording: Developing doctrine: family-first; care ladder when nearer supports cannot meet the need.

claims.claim_text: In a prosperous constitutional republic, no child should lack adequate nutrition because of circumstances beyond the child's control; implementation begins locally and the state is guarantor of last resort.
opposing_evidence: Disagreement exists over how quickly state programs should activate.
Local capacity varies widely.
claims.uncertainty: CC-DEV-082; no invented hunger statistics; links Food Security.
claims.public_wording: Developing doctrine: no child should go hungry — local first, state last resort.

claims.claim_text: Intergenerational prosperity and a Family Wealth System should make it easier for families to accumulate and transmit homes, enterprises, savings, education, skills, and community relationships — including knowledge, trust, and local institutions — without forcing co-residence.
opposing_evidence: Inheritance and housing rules involve contested tradeoffs with mobility and equity.
Nonfinancial capital is hard to measure.
claims.uncertainty: CC-DEV-081.
claims.public_wording: Developing doctrine: Family Wealth System and voluntary intergenerational connection.

claims.claim_text: Childhood investments in health, nutrition, education, housing, literacy, civic preparation, and apprenticeships are long-term national capacity investments; child flourishing should be measured by whether children are better prepared than the prior generation, with indicator values null until sourced.
opposing_evidence: Preparation comparisons across generations face measurement and cohort confounds.
claims.uncertainty: CC-DEV-083; architecture only.
claims.public_wording: Developing doctrine: children as infrastructure; measure child flourishing honestly.

claims.claim_text: Constitutional Capitalism should measure success primarily by human flourishing — whether life improved across health, family, childhood, education, civic life, ownership, resilience, environment, trust, safety, opportunity, and related domains — not by GDP, markets, spending, or profits alone; composites must not be invented before domains are sourced.
opposing_evidence: Composite indices can hide tradeoffs and create false precision.
Subjective well-being measures are contested.
claims.uncertainty: CC-DEV-088 / CC-PRIN-33; 0/17 HFI domains sourced.
claims.public_wording: Developing doctrine: Human Flourishing Index as defining benchmark — architecture, not yet measurement.

claims.claim_text: In fiscal year 2024, SNAP served an average of 41.7 million people per month — about 12.3% participation rate per USDA ERS Landscape reporting — illustrating the scale of nutrition assistance.
claims.uncertainty: Participation rate and monthly average are ERS Landscape FY2024 figures; composition and dynamics vary over time.
claims.public_wording: SNAP served about 41.7 million people per month in FY2024 (ERS) — scale context, not a claim that all are permanently disconnected from work.

claims.claim_text: SNAP caseload diversity means the program serves children, older adults, disabled people, low-wage workers, and households in temporary hardship — not solely adults permanently disconnected from work. ERS notes SNAP is not targeted to a single subgroup; in FY2023, 28% of SNAP households had earned income, and among households with children 55% had earned income.
opposing_evidence: Some subgroups within SNAP face prolonged unemployment or disconnection.
Composition shares change year to year.
claims.uncertainty: FY2023 composition figures from ERS key-statistics page; FY2024 totals from Landscape.
claims.public_wording: SNAP scale does not mean permanent work-disconnection for all recipients (ERS composition context).

claims.claim_text: No person should be abandoned when unable to meet essential needs, and no institution should trap a capable person in dependency; assistance should protect dignity, strengthen capacity, reward productive advancement, and lead toward the greatest independence reasonably possible — guaranteeing security while dismantling dependency.
opposing_evidence: Disagreement exists over how to balance unconditional floors with reciprocal expectations.
Definitions of dependency and security are contested across ideologies.
claims.uncertainty: CC-DEV-089 / CC-PRIN-34 architecture.
claims.public_wording: Developing doctrine: guarantee security; dismantle dependency traps.

claims.claim_text: Assistance systems should place recipients on distinct pathways — permanent protection, childhood/dependent care, caregiving, temporary stabilization, working-but-insecure, and capable-but-disconnected — rather than treating every recipient as having the same problem.
opposing_evidence: Pathway misclassification risk and administrative complexity.
Overlap across pathways is common in real households.
claims.uncertainty: CC-DEV-090 architecture; eligibility operations require research and pilots.
claims.public_wording: Developing doctrine: six assistance pathways — different problems, different responses.

claims.claim_text: Benefit cliffs — where lost benefits equal or exceed the earnings increase that triggered the reduction — punish advancement; Constitutional Capitalism requires that every additional hour of productive work leave a household better off through gradual phaseouts and transparent benefit-impact calculators. Exact phaseout rates require modeling.
opposing_evidence: Gradual phaseouts can raise program costs or extend participation duration.
Calculator accuracy depends on complex stacked program rules.
claims.uncertainty: Cliff definition and calculator lessons sourced; CC phaseout rates not modeled (modeling 0%).
claims.public_wording: Developing doctrine: eliminate benefit cliffs; every additional hour should leave households better off.

claims.claim_text: Fragmented assistance should be coordinated through one Human Prosperity Account and Prosperity Navigators — automate routine eligibility work; elevate humans to barrier removal, local opportunity matching, and ownership pathways — under strict privacy rules that forbid a surveillance system.
opposing_evidence: Integrated accounts raise privacy and cybersecurity risks if poorly governed.
Navigator models require workforce redesign and funding.
claims.uncertainty: CC-DEV-092/093; links public-service Automate the routine. Elevate the human.
claims.public_wording: Developing doctrine: Human Prosperity Account and Prosperity Navigators with privacy guardrails.

claims.claim_text: Before imposing participation requirements, systems must address foundations of participation (childcare, transportation, health, housing, treatment, identification, local job availability, and related barriers). CBO finds effects of work requirements and work supports vary and can be uncertain; requirements must be paired with genuine supports and independently evaluated.
opposing_evidence: Some analyses argue requirements increase employment even with limited supports.
Support packaging costs and local capacity vary.
claims.uncertainty: CBO uncertainty finding sourced; CC sanction design remains architecture.
claims.public_wording: Developing doctrine: remove barriers before requirements; evaluate requirements with supports.

claims.claim_text: Constitutional Capitalism rejects universal basic income as the organizing alternative to fragmented welfare and instead advances a Community Work Guarantee: paid local transitional public/community assignments with wages, supervision, training, worker protections, and pathways into private employment or public service — never replacing existing employees or becoming punitive work camps.
opposing_evidence: UBI advocates argue cash simplicity outperforms work-assignment administration.
Public job guarantees face displacement, stigma, and fiscal design disputes.
claims.uncertainty: CC-DEV-096 design agenda; no invented cost comparisons.
claims.public_wording: Developing doctrine: Community Work Guarantee — not UBI — as the organizing alternative.

claims.claim_text: Assistance success must not be measured by disappearing from a benefit roll alone; the scoreboard should include income, employment stability, housing, health, food security, savings, ownership, family stability, repeat enrollment, civic participation, and child well-being — asking whether the person became more capable, secure, independent, and connected.
opposing_evidence: Multi-outcome scoreboards are harder to administer than caseload metrics.
Attribution of outcomes to assistance vs economy is difficult.
claims.uncertainty: CC-DEV-102; links HFI without inventing composites.
claims.public_wording: Developing doctrine: measure exits by capability and security, not roll exit alone.

claims.claim_text: Administrative burden — including repeated reapplication, job instability, and benefit loss — is itself a source of economic risk for low-income households; fraud controls should target organized abuse without constant humiliation of lawful recipients.
opposing_evidence: Stronger verification can reduce improper payments even if it increases some burden.
Balancing integrity and access involves tradeoffs.
claims.uncertainty: ASPE economic-risk framing sourced; CC fraud architecture still design-level.
claims.public_wording: Developing doctrine: fight fraud without treating every recipient as fraudulent; reduce destabilizing burden.

claims.claim_text: The Supreme Court’s power of judicial review was confirmed in Marbury v. Madison (1803); the Court’s own account states that while judicial review was anticipated, it is not explicitly provided in the Constitution.
opposing_evidence: Scholars debate how strongly Founders anticipated judicial review and how Marbury should be read.
claims.uncertainty: Does not by itself settle who should have final constitutional authority in a redesigned system.
claims.public_wording: The source directly establishes that the Court presents Marbury as confirming judicial review and that the Constitution does not explicitly provide that function.

claims.claim_text: According to NCSL, 24 states have a statewide citizen initiative process; there is no comparable national citizen-initiative lawmaking system under the current federal Constitution.
opposing_evidence: Other trackers count 26 states with initiative or referendum or both; classifications differ by instrument.
claims.uncertainty: Use NCSL’s initiative-process count carefully; do not treat it as a national federal power.
claims.public_wording: The source directly establishes a 24-state initiative figure in NCSL’s overview; federal initiative would be a new constitutional design.

claims.claim_text: According to NCSL, 19 states allow recall elections of state officials; federal officials cannot currently be recalled under the U.S. Constitution.
opposing_evidence: Virginia’s petition-triggered removal trial is similar but not counted by NCSL as a recall-election state.
claims.uncertainty: Federal non-recall is a current-structure statement; redesign would require amendment.
claims.public_wording: The source directly establishes 19-state recall elections for state officials; federal recall is not a current constitutional tool.

claims.claim_text: Article V provides for amendments proposed by Congress or by a convention after state applications, with ratification by the states; it does not create a direct national citizen-petition route to amend the Constitution.
opposing_evidence: State-level constitutional initiatives exist separately from Article V.
claims.uncertainty: A People’s Amendment Process would be a proposed third pathway — architecture, not current law.
claims.public_wording: The Constitution’s Article V structure does not currently provide a national citizen-petition amendment ballot route.

claims.claim_text: Article III’s Good Behavior framework has been understood to support federal judges serving during good behavior; a clear system of fixed active Supreme Court terms would likely require constitutional amendment.
opposing_evidence: Some scholars argue Congress could affect Court structure short of amending tenure; that debate is unresolved and legally contested.
claims.uncertainty: CC treats durable 18-year active terms as amendment-likely design, not a claimed existing power.
claims.public_wording: Constitutional Capitalism concludes that durable fixed active Supreme Court terms should be pursued as constitutional design, not asserted as already authorized ordinary legislation.

claims.claim_text: The Supreme Court issued its first formal Code of Conduct for Justices in November 2023; enforceable independent investigation and external review of contested recusals remain a design agenda beyond that code.
opposing_evidence: The Court may argue internal processes already suffice; external enforcement raises separation-of-powers questions.
claims.uncertainty: Existence of the 2023 code is sourced; stronger enforcement is normative architecture.
claims.public_wording: The source directly establishes that a formal Justices’ Code of Conduct was issued in November 2023; Constitutional Capitalism proposes going further on enforceability.

claims.claim_text: Under the current Constitution, federal judges are not removable simply because voters disagree with their rulings; removal is generally through impeachment and conviction, not ordinary electoral recall.
opposing_evidence: Impeachment practice is rare; critics argue it is ineffective as accountability.
claims.uncertainty: CC rejects ordinary SCOTUS recall and proposes extraordinary misconduct paths as architecture.
claims.public_wording: The source directly establishes the impeachment framework for judicial removal; Constitutional Capitalism rejects ordinary partisan recall of Justices.

claims.claim_text: According to EIA, the United States produced more primary energy than it consumed in 2024 and recorded net energy exports of 9.3 quads — the highest in EIA records dating to 1949 — with energy exports reaching a record 30.9 quads.
opposing_evidence: Primary-energy surplus does not imply household affordability or public capture of export value.
claims.uncertainty: Supports capacity context for Energy Sovereignty; does not prove proposed public institutions.
claims.public_wording: The source directly establishes 2024 primary-energy surplus and record net energy exports; Constitutional Capitalism argues public return institutions are still needed.

claims.claim_text: According to EIA, U.S. electricity net generation reached a record 4.43 thousand terawatthours in 2025.
opposing_evidence: Record generation is not by itself a reliability or affordability metric.
claims.uncertainty: Context for grid modernization agenda only.
claims.public_wording: The source directly establishes record 2025 U.S. electricity net generation of 4.43 thousand TWh.

claims.claim_text: According to EIA, U.S. crude oil production set a new annual record of 13.6 million barrels per day in 2025.
opposing_evidence: Annual STEO-linked estimates may revise as monthly series finalize.
claims.uncertainty: Production record ≠ public prosperity from exports.
claims.public_wording: The source directly establishes a 13.6 million b/d U.S. crude production record in 2025.

claims.claim_text: According to the DOE Natural Gas Imports and Exports Monthly (December 2025), U.S. LNG exports by vessel totaled about 5,507 Bcf (~5.5 Tcf) year-to-date in 2025, approximately 26% above the prior-year YTD total.
opposing_evidence: Series revisions and definitional differences between DOE monthly and EIA Natural Gas Monthly are possible.
claims.uncertainty: Supports export-scale context; EIA also forecasts further LNG growth — forecasts are uncertain.
claims.public_wording: The DOE monthly report directly establishes ~5.5 Tcf YTD 2025 LNG vessel exports; export growth does not by itself create a People’s Energy Dividend.

claims.claim_text: According to EIA Energy Explained, even after becoming a total petroleum net exporter in 2020, the United States continued importing some crude oil and petroleum products to help supply domestic demand and international markets.
opposing_evidence: Net-exporter status and import composition change year to year.
claims.uncertainty: Supports sovereignty-not-autarky; page examples cite 2022 figures that EIA may refresh.
claims.public_wording: The source directly establishes that net petroleum exporter status coexists with continued crude and product imports.
